title: Finite Element Calculation of Double-Cage Skin Factors

source.citation: K. Nemeth, Periodica Polytechnica Electrical Engineering 45(3-4):245-252, 2001
source.access: openly readable on the journal site

machine.symmetry: The slot alone, per metre of length, as the paper solves it: natural boundary on the iron contour, A = 0 across the slot top.

assessors.name: skin_factor_resistance_outer
assessors.note: k_ro = R_o(50 Hz)/R_o0 = 1.2: R at 50 Hz is 1.2 times the DC value. Given to one decimal, so the tolerance is the rounding, 0.05 (4.2%).

assessors.name: skin_factor_inductance_outer
assessors.note: k_xo = L_o(50 Hz)/L_o0 = 0.98, within 1% (the rounding is 0.5%).

assessors.name: skin_factor_resistance_inner
assessors.note: k_ri = R_i(50 Hz)/R_i0 = 2.36 with the outer bar open (its eddy currents included), within 1%.

assessors.name: in_phase_current_A
assessors.quote: Current phasors calculated from the correct and the approximate equivalent circuit
assessors.location: Fig. 9, p. 252, label 43,1 on the voltage axis
assessors.note: Both bars in parallel at U = 0.1 V/m (peak, 50 Hz): the total current's component in phase with U. The correct circuit reproduces the paper's FE currents (Section 3); the approximate circuits' 36.7 and 32.4 A are not FE results.

assessors.name: lagging_current_A
assessors.quote: Current phasors calculated from the correct and the approximate equivalent circuit

assessors.note: Read at 600 dpi against the gridlines (0 A at pixel 397, 120 A at 1557): 118.8 A at the arrow tip, +-2 A for the line width. A comparator.

controls.purpose: Every element size and arc segment halved.

coverage.reproduced: The DC self and mutual inductances and DC resistances of both bars (Table 1), the four skin factors at 50 Hz (Section 5), and the in-phase current of the bars in parallel at 0.1 V/m (Fig. 9); the lagging current as a comparator.
coverage.not_reproduced: The skin factors against frequency (Fig. 8, a coarse plot), the current-density profiles (Figs. 3 and 6) and the approximate equivalent circuits.

geometry_checks.note: From Fig. 1's dimensions: a stadium of 14.4 by 25.3 mm, and an 11.4 by 22.3 mm rectangle with four 1 mm corner radii.

geometry_checks.quantity: DC resistances from the stated conductivities and areas (micro-ohm per metre)

findings: DC: the resistances agree with Table 1 within 0.05% (209.59 and 69.075 micro-ohm/m) and the outer bar's self-inductance and the mutual inductance within 0.66% and 0.61% (2.347 and 2.704 uH/m). The inner bar's self-inductance is 6.569 uH/m against 6.503 (+1.01%) and fails narrowly. All three inductances are 0.6-1.0% high and halving the mesh changes them by at most 0.05%, so the excess is not discretization; Fig. 1's dimensions are printed to 0.1 mm, and the leakage paths through the 4 mm neck and 5 mm opening are where such a reading matters most. The mutual inductance is the same from either bar to 1.5e-12.

The two bars in parallel at 0.1 V/m and 50 Hz draw an in-phase current of 43.17 A against Fig. 9's 43.1 A (+0.15%), computed from the two single-bar solves; the lagging part is 116.6 A against about 119 A read from Fig. 9 (a comparator, within its 4 A tolerance).
The outer bar's skin factors at 50 Hz pass: k_ro = 1.225 against 1.2 (inside its rounding) and k_xo = 0.983 against 0.98.

The inner bar's do not: k_ri = 4.81 against the text's 2.36 and k_xi = 0.932 against 0.955. Fig. 8, which plots the FE skin factors against frequency, reads at 50 Hz (600 dpi, against its gridlines) k_ri 4.77, k_xi 0.931, k_xo 0.984, k_xm 0.971, k_rm 2.27 and k_ro 1.19, against the model's 4.81, 0.932, 0.983, 0.971, 2.22 and 1.23. The text gives its four values for the approximate circuit 'taking the skin effect into account but ignoring R_m'; its k_ro and k_xo agree with Fig. 8, but its k_ri and k_xi are not the FE values at 50 Hz, and the paper itself calls k_ri 'too big' because of eddy currents in the outer bar. The case froze them as FE skin factors; they stay frozen and are kept as reviewed failures, and the model reproduces the paper's FE curves.
Halving the mesh changes every quantity by at most 0.054%.
retrospective: Longest: reading the scanned paper. Its tables and figure labels are not in the extracted text; the parallel-bar current is printed only on Fig. 9's axis, and the FE skin factors only in Fig. 8.

The skill lacked a check of what a quoted number is: the text's skin factors 'in this case' belong to an approximate circuit, which the paper's own Fig. 8 shows before any solve. Lesson added: before freezing a number from a sentence, find the same quantity in the paper's tables or plots and freeze the one that is the FE result.
Lessons that held: derived quantities the paper states (areas, resistances) fix ambiguous drawing details (four rounded corners; the dimension chain).

Added generically: the parallel_branches assessor (coupled conductors in parallel across one voltage, from solves that each drive one branch), and skin factors as metric_relation ratios of AC to DC solves.
